picks.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Publishing Jobs Will Adapt to AI, Not Disappear
picks.excerpt: Bloomsbury founder Nigel Newton called the idea that AI will take all publishing jobs 'rubbish'. His panel still agreed that entry-level roles may disappear, staff will need retraining and new roles will emerge.
picks.rationale: Concrete Frankfurt panel read on which publishing roles shrink (entry level) and which need retraining; broadest relevance for the teaser slot.

picks.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: EU AI Act Gives Publishers Leverage, but No Teeth
picks.excerpt: A Frankfurt panel on trust in science in the age of AI concluded that the EU AI Act helps rights holders on paper, but it has no penalties for AI developers and gives researchers no incentives.
picks.rationale: Regulatory angle on rights holders' leverage under the EU AI Act, not yet covered in the 30-day history.

picks.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Spotify Expands Audiobooks to 180 Markets
picks.excerpt: Spotify is taking its audiobook service from 22 markets to more than 180. It presents AI narration as a way to bring titles into local languages that are too small to pay for a human narrator, and self-published authors can already produce AI-narrated audiobooks through its ElevenLabs partnership.
picks.rationale: Concrete platform announcement: Spotify audiobooks go from 22 to 180+ markets, with AI narration pitched as the way to reach small-language markets. This is a new release on top of the 09-13 opening of AI narration to all authors.

picks.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: ENLIT Network Provides Support for European Literary Translation and Translators
picks.excerpt: European translation-funding bodies say literary translators currently have strong support, but AI makes their position fragile. Speakers framed AI as a dictionary-like tool that still cannot handle humor, emotion or voice.
picks.rationale: Translation-funding bodies' Frankfurt stance on AI; a distinct event from PW's 9/18 translator feature and Börsenblatt's 10/08 piece.
